title: These Ancient Sea Worms Have “Biometal” Jaws
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyThese Ancient Sea Worms Have “Biometal” JawsNot as scary as a great white shark, but the science is fascinatingDNBy David Nield3:00 PM CDT on August 4, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThere’s much in the natural world scientists and engineers can use for materials inspiration. Take, for example, the ancient bristle sea worm Perinereis cultrifera. Its jaws are made of a unique material described as a “bio-metal,” which can rival copper or silver for hardness.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 Mysterious Holes On the Seafloor Just Off the Coast of California Might Finally Have an ExplanationShareNextStayAt a fundamental level, the jaws are constructed from structural proteins and metal ions. They can be used to hold, cut, crush, and chew food, as well as serving as a defense mechanism against predators.In a study published in Biophysics Reviews, researchers took a closer look at these bio-metal jaws, probing them by creating thousands of microscopic indents in the material and running a chemical analysis of their composition, while combining these efforts with high-resolution imagery and computational models.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
